I built GHZ states of 2, 3, 4, and 5 qubits. A GHZ state puts all the qubits into one shared state. When you measure it, the qubits should all read 0 or all read 1, and each outcome should come up about half the time. I put the 4 circuits into one job with 100 shots each.

I tested the job first on the free test device sirius:mock (job 01a16050-cb87-7312-9a4d-e09e13243aad). The mock accepted the circuits and compiled them. It returns placeholder results, so its counts do not tell us anything about the physics. Then I ran the one real job you authorized on the IQM sirius QPU (job 01a16051-0a71-765b-b8bd-c5c636f8a5ed). The API reports 1.0 billed second for that job. At 0.3 credits per second, that is about 0.3 credits.

This table shows the fraction of shots where all the bits agreed. A perfect machine would score 1.00 at every size.
- 2 qubits: 0.92
- 3 qubits: 0.89
- 4 qubits: 0.88
- 5 qubits: 0.84

The score goes down as the state gets bigger. Sirius links its qubits through a central resonator. Each extra qubit adds one more two-qubit gate (a CZ through the resonator) and one more qubit to read out. Every gate and every readout has a small chance of error. A single error is enough to flip one bit and break the "all agree" pattern. More qubits mean more chances for an error, so the fraction falls step by step. That is the main reason entanglement over many qubits is hard to keep on today's hardware.

The split between all-0 and all-1 is also uneven. For example, the 5-qubit run gave 53 all-0 and 31 all-1. A qubit in state 1 can lose its energy and decay to 0 before or during readout, so errors push results toward 0. Most of the wrong shots differ from the right answer by only one bit, which matches what scattered single errors would produce. The trend is what matters here. 100 shots per size gives each fraction an uncertainty of a few percent.

The script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_664c303a-347-244/ghz_run.py, and the saved results are at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_664c303a-347-244/ghz_sirius.json.
